image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a rough, rocky substrate. The organism displays its characteristic eight overlapping dorsal plates (valves) surrounded by a textured, leathery girdle. The plates exhibit intricate growth lines and mottled brownish-grey coloration. Small white barnacles or encrustations are visible on the surrounding rock and slightly on the girdle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior end of the chiton is visible and blunt, lacking any protruding sensory structures like eyes or tentacles, consistent with chiton anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front of the animal blends smoothly into the first plate without distinct head features, matching the description.
No antennae, eyes, or other sensory organs are visible on the dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Exactly eight distinct, overlapping plates are clearly visible running from anterior to posterior along the midline.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plates embedded in tough leathery girdle that may be smooth, spiny, or hairy.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates are surrounded by a thick, textured mantle/girdle that appears leathery and granular, typical of many chiton species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates show a complex mottled pattern of browns, greys, and tans with visible radial growth lines.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal view; the ventral foot is completely occluded by the body and substrate contact.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits dorsoventrally flattened profile when clinging to surfaces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The chiton conforms tightly to the irregular rock surface, demonstrating a flattened profile adapted for adhesion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral trait not observable in a static image of an attached specimen.

To verify the structural integrity of the eight plates and ensure the girdle connects seamlessly without AI-generated melting or boundary bleeding into the rock.
To assess the realism of the micro-textures on the plates (growth lines) and the girdle, checking for smearing or unnatural repetition common in AI generation.
To ensure the chiton sits correctly on the rock surface with proper occlusion and shadowing, avoiding 'floating' artifacts.

Texture realism of the leathery girdle vs. calcareous plates
